prompt:
A wide background illustration for the menu screen of a mythology card game, made by hand like a 1993 fantasy trading-card or game-book illustration: bold, wobbly black pen-and-ink outlines around every shape, filled with thin, flat, transparent watercolour and gouache washes. Big simple flat shapes of colour with almost no shading or modelling, a little ink cross-hatching in the shadows, blotchy uneven washes with hard dried edges, splatters and visible brush marks, and the rough off-white paper texture and grain clearly showing through the paint. Naive, slightly clumsy, decorative and stylised, like an old printed card with slightly faded, misregistered colour. A limited palette of 4 or 5 colours, dark overall. Absolutely not realistic: no realistic lighting, no glow, no soft gradients, no depth of field, no fine detail or texture rendering, no oil-painting look, no 3D, no digital painting, not modern concept art. Composition for a game board: low contrast, all the interesting shapes at the edges and in the bottom corners; the centre is a calm, empty, evenly dark area, because a title, text and buttons sit on top of it. No figures or creatures in the centre. No text, no letters, no border, no frame, no logo, no signature.

Setting: the mouth of the strait of Scylla and Charybdis from Homer's Odyssey, seen from the sea in a gathering storm: on the left a towering cliff with a high dark cave; on the right a low rock with a gnarled fig tree above a churning whirlpool; the narrow passage of black water between them; lightning far off in heavy clouds; a small Greek ship's prow at the very bottom edge.
Colour: near-black storm grey to cold sea teal (#080e14 to #2a4652) with white foam and a faint lightning-white accent.
